transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-18
Start: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~74 minutes
Location: Zoom - company all-hands
Attendees: Elena Park, Marco Alvarez, Priya Desai, Samir Khan, Lina Torres, plus open Q&A from company

Summary:
- Leadership reviewed "helix" initiative (cross-functional push to tighten product/ops cadence).
- Discussed recent incident, reliability mitigations, and tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted routing.
- Agreed on hiring priorities and a conservative rollout plan for canary/traffic shaping.
- Next steps: prioritized action items for product, infra, and people.

Topics covered:
- Helix initiative overview and desired outcomes
- Incident review highlights and short/medium term mitigations
- Cost control: batching, quantization, region routing, dedicated pools
- Hiring cadence and org resourcing
- Customer & enterprise posture: SOC 2 timing, audit log retention

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Elena Park (CEO): Hey everybody, good morning, thanks for joining our helix update, we'll keep it tight, we got a lot to cover and then open q and a. um Marco, quick microstate of infra?
[00:18] Marco Alvarez (CTO): yeah, morning. so we've been tracking that spike last week, the incident, turns out it was a combo of an autoscaler bug and a kernel selection mismatch on the newest gpu nodes, uh, and that caused very uneven tail latency, and then a the fallback routing didn't kick fast enough.
[00:35] Speaker 4 (Engineering lead - Samir): to add, the KV cash — sorry, KV cache priming logic was racing with the cold starts, so lots of cache misses when we hit long sequences, so token costs spiked.
[00:50] Elena: ok, that's the gist. i'm hoping we can walk through short-term mitigations first, then product priorities. Priya?
[01:02] Priya Desai (Head of Product): yeael, so helix is meant to be the cross-team cadence — product builds, infra optimizations, and ops guardrails. high level targets: reduce P99 latency by 20%, keep per-token costs flat, and cut incident recovery time in half by Q3. those are our north stars.
[01:25] [01:25] Lina Torres (Head of People): and tangentially hiring: we need to line up three infra senior ICs and two SREs by end of Q2 to hit these numbers, otherwise we won't make the throughput work without cost overruns.
[01:40] Marco: yea the capacity plan is tight, and our vendor quotes for extra reserved capacity are... not great, so we need to balance dedicated pools versus smarter routing.
[01:54] [01:54] Audience Question (Speaker X): hi could you clarify what dedicated pools mean for existing hosted customers, any pricing changes?
[02:03] Elena: good question — in short, dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, it's opt-in for enterprise customers, pricing considered as a monthly commit. won't change hosted pricing for existing users. we'll send a short FAQ later.
[02:20] Priya: also important, for helix we want more canary control: traffic shaping by region, by tenant tier, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if latency SLOs break.
[02:38] Marco: the automatic fallback needs to be model-aware though; not every variant has the same function-calling or structured-output behavior, so we'll need compatibility checks. some of the autogen tests failed because of that.
[02:56] Samir: yes and there's a product-quality tradeoff — fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant gives cost savings but sometimes the hallucination rate nudges up, which our evals catch but customers might see.
[03:13] Elena: we need to balance unit economics with trust metrics. Priya, keep eval thresholds tight.
[03:21] Priya: noted.
[03:24] [03:24] Marco: quick point on the incident root cause: the new kernel selector we pushed assumes consistent sequence length distribution. during a customer experiment, sequence lengths skewed long and that pushed a codepath we hadn't exercised in staging. staging datasets didn't cover the churn.
[03:42] Speaker 7 (Product PM): so we should expand staging replay and add stress tests for long sequence tails, yes?
[03:48] Marco: exactly. we'll add a sequence-tail stress harness.
[03:51] [04:00] Audience (Volunteer): will this affect the private deploys and VPC customers?
[04:06] Samir: private customers are on a different upgrade cadence, but the same runtime code flows. for private we can schedule staggered upgrades and extra canaries since they control their infra. the main worry is the private on-prem customers that are air-gapped — their kernel backports take longer.
[04:25] Elena: we'll capture those timelines separately with CSMs.
[04:28] [04:30] Lina: hiring note — compensation for the infra hires is tight, we've got to move offers by May 3rd to meet joiners in June. otherwise Q3 headcount will slip.
[04:43] Priya: on product roadmap, the helix MVP is three features: 1) traffic shaping UI in console, 2) explicit model-variant compatibility checks, 3) improved rollout telemetry and tracing per request. those are our first deliverables.
[05:03] Marco: on telemetry, we need token-level tracing that ties back to route config and to the KV priming state. right now traces are coarse.
[05:13] Samir: that telemetry will also let us tune batching better — we can identify request shapes that benefit from bigger batch windows. bigger batches reduce cost but up latency for short requests; so routing rules need to be aware.
[05:30] [05:30] Audience (Q): do we have new SOC 2 timelines?
[05:35] Elena: good timing — audit kickoff is next month, target completion end of Q3. Lina and security will share specifics. we'll publish an FAQ.
[05:44] Lina: security readiness is in parallel; we have two key gaps: long-term log retention policy and more formal RBAC in the console. both are on the board for May sprints.
[05:57] [05:57] Priya: quick product concern — if we enforce stricter RBAC it may change how we do customer-level rollouts for early access features. need product and security handshake.
[06:09] Marco: yes, and for the canary we need a fallback policy that prioritizes continuity over feature parity — meaning if a canary fails we keep customers online on last-known-good model variant.
[06:22] Samir: on the ops side, the short term mitigation is to revert the autoscaler change for the hot path and add safer thresholds; medium term is to revamp our kernel selector testing and expand mix of real traffic in staging.
[06:36] [06:36] Audience: any customer impact notices sent?
[06:40] Elena: we sent a brief to affected customers with a high-level postmortem and said we were executing mitigations. follow-up will include a more detailed postmortem and timelines.
[06:50] [07:00] Priya: ok timeline for helix: sprints 1-2 (2 weeks) finish telemetry and canary control, sprints 3-4 (4 more weeks) ship console UI and rollout compatibility checks. we want an internal canary by mid-May and public canary in late May if hiring and infra align.
[07:18] Marco: about cost optimization — two levers: smarter batching and model quantization recommendations surfaced in console. the Optimize toolkit will suggest quantization profiles and batching windows per route. we should be careful: not all models are safe at 4-bit, and we need evals for each customer workload.
[07:36] Samir: that said, we can start with non-critical tenants for aggressive quantization to get baseline numbers.
[07:45] [07:50] Audience (Question): are we changing pricing for embeddings?
[07:55] Elena: not today. any pricing adjustments would come with clear customer comms; our priority is stability and predictable unit economics.
[08:05] [08:10] Priya: a small but important ask: product will need example prompts and eval criteria from sales and solutions so our regression alerts are meaningful — please send the top 10 prompt sets by next Tuesday.
[08:24] Lina: people update — org health looks good in most teams but infra is stretched. hiring freeze lifted for critical roles; recruiters will prioritize infra and SRE. also we want to remind managers about offer flexibility for counteroffers.
[08:42] [08:45] Audience: are we going to centralize the benchmark sheets?
[08:49] Marco: yes, a single benchmark spreadsheet will be the source of truth; infra will own it with read perms broadly but edit perms limited. we'll put it in the shared drive and link in the console docs.
[08:59] Samir: action on incident owner mapping: we'll publish a runbook with clear owners for autoscale, kernel selection, and KV priming.
[09:10] [09:10] Priya: ok let's take live questions.
[09:15] Audience Q1: will this change our roadmap for Dedicated customers?
[09:20] Marco: Dedicated still gets priority for capacity; any region routing changes will be backwards compatible. Dedicated customers can still pin versions and we will offer a rollback window.
[09:31] Audience Q2: what's the customer-facing SLA change?
[09:35] Elena: no SLA change today; we will only adjust SLAs with clear product and infra readiness and after legal signs off.
[09:44] Audience Q3: can we get an incident dashboard?
[09:50] Samir: yes, we will publish an internal incident dashboard and a high-level customer-facing timeline for affected customers.
[10:00] [10:00] Elena: brief recap — Priya product plan and eval thresholds; Samir postmortem and runbook; Marco hardware/cost review; Lina hiring and offers. big ask: leaders to empower their teams to escalate when telemetry shows odd tails.
[10:18] Marco: last thing, competitor note: BigCloudAI rolled out a cheaper dedicated option last month; their fallback behavior isn't as mature as ours but their price looks aggressive. watch for sales objections and we'll prepare battlecards.
[10:33] Priya: and FastServe is pushing a private-edge pitch in EMEA, we should coordinate partner messaging.
[10:40] Elena: alright, thanks everyone. we'll post slides and the canary plan. meeting closed.

Post-meeting notes:
- Slides: link (internal) - "Helix initiative overview and canary plan"
- Shared artifacts: incident summary (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), hiring slate (link).
- Tone: constructive, operationally focused, few tense questions about cost and hiring but consensus on next steps.

End of transcript.
